headline: [Hormuz Blasts!] Iran Says [3 Oil Tankers] Hit Mines and Caught Fire
sub: Iran says ships used banned routes
caption:
🚨 BREAKING: Iran Says 3 Oil Tankers Hit Mines and Caught Fire in Hormuz

Iran's navy and Revolutionary Guards said on Saturday that three oil tankers hit naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire. Iran says the ships had switched off their tracking systems and were using routes it does not allow.

🔹 Iran said two of the tankers were hit in the south of the strait, one of them a supertanker. A third was hit east of the strait. The ships' names and any casualties were not given, and there is no independent confirmation yet.
🔹 The UN told the Security Council on Friday that at least 25 seafarers have been killed in and around Hormuz since the war began in February.
🔹 Shipping through Hormuz is about 65% below pre-war levels, the UK's maritime agency (UKMTO) says. The US military says it has cleared the main routes of mines.

💬 How do you think this will affect oil prices? 👇

Sources: AFP, Al Jazeera, Middle East Eye

headline: [Historic First!] Trump, Xi and Putin to Hold [Three-Way Summit] in China
sub: Nuclear arms and Iran war on the agenda
caption:
🌍 Historic First: Trump, Xi and Putin to Hold Three-Way Summit in China

The White House said on Friday that US President Donald Trump will meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, China, next week. It will be the first three-way meeting of the three leaders, held on the sidelines of the APEC summit.

🔹 White House spokesperson Olivia Wales said Trump will discuss "the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world". The New START nuclear treaty between the US and Russia expired in February.
🔹 US officials said the Iran war will also be discussed, but Ukraine will not. A senior US official told Reuters: "We do not expect to get to any kind of agreement."
🔹 The APEC leaders' meeting runs on 18-19 November. Moscow and Beijing had not commented when the plan was announced.

💬 Do you think this meeting can lead to a nuclear deal? 👇

Sources: Al Jazeera, Euronews, AFP

headline: [Big Ruling!] ICC Stops Probe Into Alleged Crimes by [US Troops] in Afghanistan
sub: Court will now focus on the Taliban
caption:
⚖️ Big Ruling: ICC Stops Probe Into Alleged Crimes by US Troops in Afghanistan

Judges at the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague have ordered the prosecutor to stop investigating alleged crimes by American troops in Afghanistan. The ruling was issued on Thursday and made public on Friday.

🔹 The court's Afghanistan inquiry will now focus only on alleged crimes by the Taliban since 2021. A separate probe into the ISIS group in Khorasan (ISKP) was also closed.
🔹 The judges cited "significant limitations to the Prosecution's ability to conduct its investigations and secure evidence." The US troops part of the probe had been inactive since 2021.
🔹 The prosecutor's office says it has already appealed. Arrest warrants for four Taliban leaders remain in force. The US is not an ICC member and has put sanctions on court staff.

💬 Should international courts be able to investigate any country's soldiers? 👇

Sources: Reuters, AP, Al Jazeera

#GlobalEye #ICC #Afghanistan #Taliban #USA #WorldNews
photo_needed: International Criminal Court (ICC) building in The Hague, with the ICC sign/logo clearly visible. A big, clear, landscape photo works best.
